fact: The policy says government data shall be stored in unified, cloud-enabled data centres with redundancies in designated locations, names the State Information Technology Agency (SITA) as the authority to source data infrastructure and cloud services for government, and says departments and entities shall prioritise cloud as the primary option for new ICT procurement; no list of providers or of specific hosting is given in this text (date is the document's published date).

fact: ENSafrica reports the DCDT officially published the National Data and Cloud Policy (Government Gazette No. 50741) on 31 May 2024 under section 3(1) of the Electronic Communications Act, 2005, applying to national and provincial government, organs of state and the private sector.

ENSafrica says the policy aims to migrate all government IT services to the cloud via decentralised private providers, requires government data centre infrastructure to be in the country, names no government cloud or provider list, and still needs implementation through consultation with SITA and departments (as of 10 June 2024).

National Treasury's reply of 10 September 2024 refers to the 'National Policy on Data and Cloud (2024)' and says Treasury considered its implications and plans to convert its 2016 IFMS licences to cloud-based.
